content:
The University of Waterloo runs one of Canada's largest research-graduate portfolios — quantum computing, AI, robotics, nanotechnology, vision and imaging among them. For international students the key fact is this: most research-based funding at Waterloo flows through your supervisor's grants, with central awards layered on top. Understanding that mix is what separates funded offers from expensive ones.

How funding is built at Waterloo

A typical funded research master's or PhD offer combines:

  • Research assistantship (RA) — paid from your supervisor's grants; the backbone of most packages
  • Teaching assistantship (TA) — paid work marking or running tutorials
  • Scholarships/awards — entrance awards such as the International Master's Award of Excellence (IMAE), valued at $2,500 per term for up to 6 terms, or graduate scholarships (TGS/UGS)
  • Doctoral awards — the Canada Graduate Research Scholarships–Doctoral (CGRS-D, tri-agency) at $40,000 per year for 3 years (restricted to Canadian citizens and permanent residents)

What international students actually receive

International research master's students admitted to research-based programs are the target group for the IMAE ($2,500/term, maximum 6 terms). Doctoral packages are usually larger: many STEM departments guarantee international PhD students a funding package in the region of $25,000–$40,000 per year through a combination of RA, TA and awards, while tuition for international students remains substantially higher than domestic — so a fully funded offer letter matters more at Waterloo than almost anywhere in Europe.

Always ask the department two questions before accepting: what is the guaranteed funding level per term, and what portion depends on winning an internal award? The answer should be in writing on your offer.

Finding a funded position: professor first, portal second

Because RA money sits with professors, the application route that works at Waterloo is the professor-first route:

  1. Identify labs whose recent papers match your background — Waterloo groups such as the CVISS/iNDT Lab advertise research positions directly.
  2. Email a short, specific approach message; our supervisor email templates work unchanged for Canadian labs.
  3. Only after a professor signals interest should you pay the application fee and submit the official portal application — many funded offers begin as an informal lab conversation.
  4. Apply by the program deadline if you also want award consideration: most fall-2027 funding decisions are made from files complete by December–February.

How Waterloo compares

Against the UK stipend model (currently about £20,000/year) a funded Waterloo PhD package is competitive, but against salaried European PhDs (Germany, Switzerland, Netherlands) the numbers look different once tuition is counted. International PhD tuition at Waterloo is roughly CAD $15,000/year on top of living costs in the Kitchener–Waterloo region — hence the advice above: get the funding guarantee in writing, and read our self-funded PhD guide for the fallback options.

faqs.question: Are international students funded at the University of Waterloo?
faqs.answer: Most research-based international graduate students are funded through a package combining a supervisor research assistantship, teaching assistantship and awards. The level varies by department — science and engineering PhD packages commonly reach $25,000–$40,000 per year, while professional and course-based programs are usually self-funded. Always get the guaranteed figure in writing on your offer.

faqs.question: What is the International Master's Award of Excellence (IMAE)?
faqs.answer: The IMAE is Waterloo's principal entrance award for international master's students entering research-based programs, valued at $2,500 per term for a maximum of 6 terms (up to $15,000 total). Eligible students are considered automatically or via the graduate award application — check your department's process.

faqs.question: Can international students get the $40,000 CGRS-D doctoral scholarship?
faqs.answer: No — the Canada Graduate Research Scholarships–Doctoral ($40,000/year for 3 years) from NSERC, SSHRC and CIHR are restricted to Canadian citizens and permanent residents. International PhD students at Waterloo are funded through RA/TA packages and international-specific awards instead.

faqs.question: How do I find a funded research position at Waterloo?
faqs.answer: Professor first, portal second. Identify labs matching your background, email a short specific approach (our supervisor email templates work for Canadian labs too), and submit the official application once a professor signals interest. Many funded offers begin as an informal lab conversation — see the CVISS/iNDT Lab listing on this site for a live example.

faqs.question: When should I apply for fall 2027 entry at Waterloo?
faqs.answer: Program deadlines for fall 2027 mostly fall between December 2026 and February 2027, and award consideration favours early complete files. Start contacting supervisors in September–November 2026, and check the official graduate calendar for your specific program's deadline.
